title: Vector Pulse pricing experiment and QSA intake: dynamic per-vector pulses for embeddings & rerank
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: validate a 'Vector Pulse' billing construct that charges for active inference pulses (micro-batches) instead of strict per-vector units, to surface lower invoices for spiky rerank workloads while capturing cost savings from batching and KV cache reuse. Deliverables: experiment plan, mock billing calculator, QSA intake checklist and proposed contract language for enterprise commitments.
background: Current feedback from several enterprise customers and solutions engineers: per-vector metering is straightforward but penalizes high-cardinality, bursty rerank calls where batching/KV cache yields lower marginal cost. Existing batch-slot concepts are complex for customers to reason about. We want a middle ground: charge per 'pulse' (a micro-batch event) with a per-vector floor and burst discounts tied to observed batching efficiency. This ticket coordinates PM work + QSA intake and legal signal for draft contract language.
hypothesis: If we bill rerank-heavy and batched embeddings as 'Vector Pulse' units with a pulse base fee plus a per-vector incremental fee and an automated burst discount after a rolling threshold, then customers with bursty traffic will see 10-40% lower effective cost while Redwood preserves unit economics via measured batching and KV cache multipliers.
success_metrics: 1) 20%+ reduction in invoice for representative bursty rerank customer cohort (n=8) during pilot; 2) no >5% negative revenue impact vs forecast across committed customers; 3) clear improvement in customer NPS on billing clarity for test cohort; 4) implementable QSA answers for top 10 enterprise queries.
experiment_design: 1) Select 8 pilot customers (mix of AI-native and enterprise) who opt into the experiment. 2) Run parallel pricing simulation on historical telemetry for 90 days to estimate delta. 3) Implement a server-side simulator that calculates 'pulse' counts by grouping requests using a 50ms micro-batch window and tagging how many vectors processed. 4) Compute three model variants for pricing: A) pulse-base + per-vector (no burst discount), B) pulse-base + per-vector + sliding burst discount (5-25%), C) hybrid with quantized pulse credits (monthly roll-forward). 5) Run 30-day live pilot under opt-in conditions with transparent billing mock invoices before committing. 6) Collect telemetry and customer feedback and run econ analysis.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal econ sim and legal/QSA intake (this ticket). Phase 1: shadow billing for selected pilots and internal engineering telemetry validation. Phase 2: opt-in pilots with mock invoices and revised docs. Phase 3: GA experiment with configurable controls in Console for 'pulse window' and burst thresholds. GA rollout gated on SLO for revenue delta and QSA closure.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers misinterpret pulse as opaque and see invoice variance. Mitigation: publish an online simulator in Console and provide detailed mock invoices. Risk: Billing system complexity and edge cases causing meter divergence. Mitigation: build a reconciliation shim and require a 2-week shadow run. Risk: QSA flags around accounting of processed vectors (auditability). Mitigation: store batch-level telemetry with signatures and provide audit endpoints for enterprise customers.
qsa_actions: 1) Compile answers for standard QSA about metering accuracy, data retention for batch telemetry, and access controls. 2) Provide a sample SIEM export and proof of provenance for pulse aggregation. 3) Coordinate with Security to fill in QSA sections: metering architecture, KMS usage for invoicing blobs, and retention policy for telemetry (90 days).
contract_suggestions: - Insert new addendum: 'Vector Pulse Billing' that defines pulse, pulse window, and burst discount schedule. - Add reconciliation clause requiring 14-day shadow billing prior to finalizing committed volumes. - Add audit rights limited to meter proofs and redacted telemetry (PII stripped). - Offer optional SLA credit if measured batching efficiency drops below agreed threshold.
